article_notes: Retrospective (2000-2009) and prospective (2009-2013) records of 363 smear-positive dogs from the University of Zambia clinic and two private practices in Lusaka. Species by semi-nested PCR in 62 prospective dogs: B. gibsoni 20, B. rossi 5, mixed 37. Outcome (death) is not reported by group. Severity measures used: hospitalised vs outpatient (treatment intensity) and degree of anaemia (PCV and PCV-based grades). Comparisons by species and breed use PCV as the outcome. Table 2 compares haematology between species groups with no test and with species as the grouping, not severity; not extracted. The hospitalised vs outpatient PCV result is self-contradictory (text says no significant difference, P = 0.030 printed).

severity_definitions.label: hospitalised vs outpatient
severity_definitions.definition: Dogs hospitalised (overnight to 21 days) vs dogs treated as outpatients.
severity_definitions.comparison_group: outpatients (n not printed; the rest of 363)
severity_definitions.quote: Of the dogs diagnosed with Babesia, 41.9% (152/363) were hospitalised, whilst the rest were treated on an outpatient basis.

severity_definitions.label: degree of anaemia (PCV; severe / moderate / mild / non-anaemic)
severity_definitions.definition: Anaemia graded by PCV: severe <15%, moderate 15-30%, mild >30-37%, non-anaemic >37% (modified Reyers et al. 1998 via Jacobson, and Tvedten and Weiss); PCV also used as a continuous measure of anaemia severity.
severity_definitions.quote: Dogs with PCV less than 15% were considered as severely anaemic, and those with PCV 15–30 as moderately anaemic, those with PCV >30–37 as mildly anaemic, and those with PCV >37% as nonanaemic.
severity_definitions.definition_source: modification of Reyers et al. (1998) cited by Jacobson, combined with Tvedten and Weiss

associations.quote: There was no significant difference in the proportion of anaemia and PCV in dogs that were hospitalised and those that were not (ANOVA: F 1, 362 = 5.25; P = 0.030; hospitalised mean PCV ± SD = 15.36 ± 6.18, outpatient mean PCV ± SD = 21.36 ± 7.60).
associations.note: Text says no significant difference but prints P = 0.030 (below the stated alpha of 0.05), so significance is unclear. The proportion of anaemic dogs is covered by the same sentence with no separate numbers.

associations.statistic: transfusion in 6 of 7 transfused dogs being hospitalised; chi-square = 5.636, df = 1
associations.quote: Hospitalised dogs were more likely to be the ones given a blood transfusion than outpatient cases (χ ^2 = 5.636, df = 1, and P = 0.018)
associations.note: Transfusion is itself a treatment-intensity measure, so this row partly reflects the definition. The authors note the outpatient cell had only one case (chi-square assumption not met). Counts 6 of 7 are from Results 3.4 para 2.

associations.statistic: proportion of severely anaemic dogs did not differ by age class; values only in Figure 3
associations.quote: There were also no differences in proportions of dogs showing severe anaemia by age class (Figure 3).
associations.note: No test statistic or P printed; methods state chi-square for proportions. Per-age-class proportions only in a figure.

associations.marker_as_reported: Babesia species (B. rossi single, B. gibsoni single, mixed)
associations.statistic: mean PCV ± SD: B. rossi 10.67 ± 1.53, B. gibsoni 16.11 ± 6.81, mixed infection 20.15 ± 9.94; ANOVA F 2,60 = 2.03
associations.quote: but the differences were not significant (ANOVA: F 2, 60 = 2.03; P = 0.15; B. rossi mean PCV ± SD 10.67 ± 1.53; B. gibsoni mean PCV ± SD 16.11 ± 6.81; mixed infection PCV ± SD 20.15 ± 9.94)
associations.note: PCV (degree of anaemia) is the severity measure. Single B. rossi lowest PCV, mixed infection highest (co-infection with lower anaemia); direction 'mixed' because there is no single severe group. Hb said to follow the same pattern, without separate test numbers.

associations.marker_as_reported: breed (mongrel vs exotic breeds and crosses)
associations.statistic: mean PCV ± SD exotic 18.28 ± 8.94 vs mongrel 18.5 ± 9.62; ANOVA F 1,362 = 0.02
associations.quote: There were no statistical differences in PCV between mongrels and exotic breeds and their crosses (ANOVA: F 1, 362 = 0.02; P = 0.876; exotic mean PCV ± SD 18.28 ± 8.94, mongrel mean PCV ± SD 18.5 ± 9.62).
associations.note: PCV (degree of anaemia) is the severity measure; groups are breed groups.

associations.statistic: Pearson r = 0.231 between PCV and rectal temperature
associations.quote: There was a weak positive significant correlation between PCV and rectal body temperature (r = 0.231, P = 0.017).
associations.note: Higher temperature goes with higher PCV, i.e. with less severe anaemia, hence negative_association with severity. Number of dogs in the correlation not printed.
